24.en: The @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.DuUfJmvyY53xYN2V]{Cruciator}, a chirurgeon skilled in the knowledge of the body and repairing injuries of the flesh, provides the invaluable service of managing all minor medicae issues and devastating injuries without needing to show vulnerability to unknown quantities. Many in this role are seen as cold and calculating, but to an Inquisitor, this is a prized quality; the colder the Cruciator’s demeanour, the better they are at fulfilling their duty without complication.

28.en: Cruciators are, however, far more than just adept healers. With all of the Inquisition’s staple dedication to wiping the Imperium clean of heretical corruption, Cruciators turn their steady hands to investigation, interrogation, and drawing out earnest repentance as readily as any acolyte. Their specific knowledge of the Human body (or xenos in rare subjects) increases their abilities in close combat and improves their chances at coaxing even the most recalcitrant of heretics into offering valuable information.

32.en: Inquisitors source their Cruciators from all corners of the Imperium. Some might have trained within the Priesthood of Mars as a Biologis, requisitioned for their knowledge of both man and machine. Others are drawn from traditional chirurgeon roles, such as the Orders Hospitaller, the Administratum’s Officio Medicae, or even the Astra Militarum, where their skills have been tempered by front-line duty. But beyond a team’s need for medicae support, a Cruciator can serve as a skilled @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.ZjtoAVYHcBRBAh7H]{Querent} or @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.UMXPdNRFRDLXnSBj]{Xenologist}, if they have the grit and detachment needed to get their hands dirty.

36.en: Those chosen for this role should have an insatiable thirst for knowledge. The compact you make with your Inquisitor affords you incredible carte blanche to explore the absolute limits of Human anatomy and design, far beyond the sanctioned learnings offered to most within the Imperium. That’s to say nothing of the mutants, xenos, and daemons you may otherwise encounter. What your Inquisitor expects in return is a trusted acolyte who can act as a versatile chirurgeon, interrogator, or even poisoner or researcher.
